description: NestJS and Angular SaaS starter with intentionally attacker-reachable server and cross-service vulnerability flows.

vulnerabilities.description: The auth continuation endpoint redirects to an attacker-controlled next URL after a login or invitation flow.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: An attacker can make users follow a trusted SaaS URL that redirects to an arbitrary external destination.

vulnerabilities.description: The invite-preview endpoint compiles a caller-supplied Dot template instead of treating the invitation text as data.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: An attacker can execute template expressions in the Nest process and access values exposed to the template context.

vulnerabilities.description: The Nest invite-message endpoint interpolates an attacker-controlled name into a string response that is served to the Angular client.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: An attacker can inject markup into an invitation preview response and execute script when it is rendered as trusted HTML.

vulnerabilities.description: The Angular registration page fetches the invite-message response and marks it trusted with DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml before binding it to innerHTML.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: An attacker can carry crafted invitation markup from the Nest API into the Angular registration origin and execute script.

vulnerabilities.description: The admin user-export endpoint passes the requested export format into a shell command launched by the users service.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: An authenticated administrator-shaped attacker can execute arbitrary shell commands with the API process privileges.

vulnerabilities.description: The admin export search interpolates the search parameter into a raw TypeORM SQL query.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: An attacker with access to the export search can alter the query and read or manipulate database data.
